title: Mri brain side view
author: Oliver Stollmann
notes: Sagittal MRI, face/anterior left. No visible patient identifiers. Good for sagittal plane, corpus callosum, brainstem, cerebellum. Source grants all uses with credit.

title: MRI Brain T2 Cor (16)
author: 511KeV
notes: Posterior coronal T2 section. Good for coronal plane recognition. Do not label this as a literal exterior front view. No laterality labels; avoid left/right hemisphere quiz.

title: Brain-T2-axial
author: Sean Novak
notes: Axial T2-weighted MRI, anterior at image top. Good for axial/transverse recognition; avoid laterality question because R/L markers absent. An axial section is not an exterior superior view.

title: Human brain lateral view
author: John A. Beal, PhD, LSU Health Sciences Center Shreveport
notes: Lateral specimen photograph; anterior left. Marker positions verified with companion labeled photo. Frontal 26%,54%; parietal 60%,35%; temporal 64%,64%; occipital 90%,51%; cerebellum 79%,86%.

title: Human brain midsagittal cut
author: John A. Beal, PhD, LSU Health Sciences Center Shreveport
notes: Midsagittal specimen photograph, anterior right. Marker positions verified with companion labeled photo: thalamus 51.6%,55.6%; hypothalamus 54.8%,62.8%; pons 38.2%,73.3%; cerebellum 24.5%,66.3%; medulla 26.2%,84.4%. Corpus callosum approximate center 53%,44%. Hippocampus is not exposed by a true midsagittal cut.

title: Brain autopsy top view
author: Jensflorian
notes: Actual superior specimen photo after formalin fixation. Two cerebral hemispheres and central longitudinal fissure visible. Good for superior view, fissure, gyri/sulci; avoid orientation/laterality quiz without independent markers.
